name: Place de la Concorde
overview: Place de la Concorde is the largest public square in Paris, located between the Champs-Élysées and the Tuileries Garden. This historic octagonal square features the ancient Luxor Obelisk and stunning fountains.
history: Originally called Place Louis XV, it was redesigned in 1755 and became Place de la Révolution during the French Revolution, where over 1,300 people were guillotined including King Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette. It was renamed Place de la Concorde in 1795.
highlights: 3,300-year-old Luxor Obelisk from Luxor Temple, Egypt
Two magnificent Fontaines de la Concorde
Eight statues representing major French cities
Views of Champs-Élysées, Tuileries, and Madeleine Church
tips: Be very careful crossing - heavy traffic from all directions. Best viewed during Toot Bus tour or from Tuileries Garden side. Evening illumination is spectacular. Free to visit and photograph.
